 W.A. Nos.1124 & 693 of 2025  5  2025:KER:37367  JUDGMENT Dr. A.K.Jayasankaran Nambiar, J.

Both these appeals arises out of the common judgment dated 27.01.2025 of the learned Single Judge disposing the writ petitions that they preferred challenging a land acquisition proceedings by holding that while the appellants herein were not justified in challenging the acquisition proceedings per se, their rights to challenge the computation of compensation and to seek a fresh determination of the market value/ compensation under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as '2013 Act') had to be safeguarded.
2.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The learned Single Judge, therefore, while disposing the writ petition made it clear that the contention of the appellants challenging the validity of the award is not accepted, and that the same would stand rejected.

Thereafter, while reserving the liberty of the appellants to raise their objections with regard to the computation effected by the Collector while passing the award, the learned Single Judge held the acquisition and the passing of the award to be valid except for the limited interference on the question of quantification of the compensation, as the same was done without hearing the appellants.

It was further made clear that the appellants would not resist any other steps to be taken by the respondents as regards the acquired land and that no claims other than the one directed to be considered would be entertained at the instance of the appellants.
We have heard Sri.S.M. Prem, the learned counsel for the appellants and Smt.N. Sudha, the learned Government Pleader on behalf of the respondents.

4. We note from the submissions of Sri.S.M. Prem, the learned counsel for the appellants that the apprehension of the appellants is essentially with regard to the effective reconsideration and determination of the market value/compensation to be paid to the appellants in accordance with the 2013 Act.

While the impugned judgment of the learned Single Judge makes it clear that save for the limited aspect of redetermination of compensation, the award passed would otherwise be valid, we are of the view that in order to avoid any confusion, the judgment of the learned Single Judge can be modified to the limited extent of stating that the award passed in the instant cases shall stand set aside so that the Collector can pass a fresh award after taking note of the objections raised by the appellants on the limited issue of quantification of compensation in relation to the lands acquired V.Aravind vs State Of Kerala on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129384524/
4 from them.
